tracks.title: Proof architecture & prime windows
tracks.question: What signal would an off-line zero force, and where does the arithmetic bound it?
tracks.route: Original localized Landau → prime ramps → readable remainder
tracks.finding: The two source editions share a smoothed observable and a nonvanishing endpoint. Coefficient, quantifier, and scale changes govern what each interface transports.

studies.title: Initial five probes
studies.detail: Localized Landau, error scaling, exceptional intervals, covolumes and proof dependencies.

studies.title: Localized window replay
studies.detail: Rebuilds 30 modules for the analytic implication from one-sided windows to a zero-free region.

studies.title: Stable-range theta lifts
studies.detail: Traces why the arithmetic argument uses two nonzero theta lifts.

studies.title: Siegel–Weil constant term
studies.detail: Follows the normalization and rank split behind the factors one and two.

studies.title: A zero and the prime windows
studies.detail: Traces the smoothed prime observable and tests manufactured signals and actual prime powers.

studies.title: Cofinal endpoints

studies.title: Exceptional bands
studies.detail: Measures positive prime mass inside bands and traces what survives a failed exceptional-integer test.

studies.title: Windows and prime remainder
studies.detail: Compares the original cofinal windows with the readable eventual remainder bound.

related.title: Common interfaces

related.title: Joint critical edition
related.detail: Derives the positive-coefficient consequence at fixed exponent slack and reconciles the original target-four mass with the matched readable convention.

tracks.title: Arithmetic witnesses & exceptions
tracks.question: Which conclusions keep the same field, host, retained set, and exceptional data?
tracks.route: Joint PairRow → slot centers → two selections across a gap
tracks.finding: Distinguishing existence from identification explains why a bound can hold even when the record cannot decide whether a particular integer belongs to its chosen exception list.

studies.title: One PairRow and one host
studies.detail: Follows the exceptional interval and prime row into the same arithmetic core.

studies.title: Slot three, specified centers
studies.detail: At cutoff 64, two valid single-center witnesses disagree on whether weight 1 is exceptional.

studies.title: Class ascent over Q(ζ₃)
studies.detail: Discharges the class-number assumption and formalizes non-unique exceptional sets.

studies.title: Selection on one retained host
studies.detail: Tests coset shares and character bounds on the same set.

studies.title: Two selections across a gap
studies.detail: Spells out the coherence and crossover conditions needed for a prescribed gap.

studies.title: Fixed slot at seven
studies.detail: Shows vanishing at fixed slots 3 and 7 and isolates the moving field tests at 2.

related.title: Recovering the arithmetic witness
related.detail: Traces a fixed readable datum, its prime partition, and the constraints of transporting the same original witness.

related.title: Selected places and signed indices
related.detail: Checks capacity and conditional coset transport at q₀ = 18480 and d = 9239.

tracks.title: Orbit losses & recovery
tracks.question: How much of the original odd-position allowance can the fallback gain recover?
tracks.route: Weighted orbit test → actual gain → sharp stationary 64-cycle
tracks.finding: The 10.1190% stationary 64-cycle optimum and the supremum over growing compatible families quantify different constructions.

studies.title: Weighted orbit test
studies.detail: Two retained sets with equal coset shares can have opposite weighted orbit outcomes.

studies.title: Bad-orbit costs
studies.detail: Follows one weighted orbit change into the original omission and prime estimates.

studies.title: Which primes are served?
studies.detail: Follows the effective weights for the high inert primes and the same host’s analytic bounds.

studies.title: Odd-position charge
studies.detail: Sharpens the principal conductor-one local allowance and tests compatible selections.

studies.title: Actual gain against the fallback
studies.detail: Holds prime, orbit, and lift fixed and compares the clipped competing gains.

studies.title: Recovery under the original score
studies.detail: Includes a compatible long-orbit construction recovering 2/45 of its odd-position allowance.

studies.title: Recovery frontier
studies.detail: Separates an asymptotic supremum over compatible choices from finite uniform templates.

studies.title: A hand certificate for ten percent
studies.detail: A 64-cycle construction guarantees 12087/120814 for every labeling in its stated setting.

studies.title: 64-cycle optimization
studies.detail: Matches the bounds for stationary profiles in the specified host construction at 10.11902517624%.

tracks.title: Same-set Frobenius & gain
tracks.question: Can the original selector admit two odd partners on the same set, and can their gain survive the original window charges?
tracks.route: Spacing → two odd partners → b′/4 row premium → τ and io
tracks.finding: The newest study keeps the weighted host and retained set fixed through an existential prime-and-orbit selection. Six Lean components check local and transport steps. The final late selection is written.

studies.title: Original versus compact spacing
studies.detail: Finds a rank obstruction at fixed d and contrasts the original local clauses with compact uniqueness.

studies.title: Frobenius premium in the arithmetic window
studies.detail: Traces the lift-summed premium through original tauAt and ioAt on one weighted host.

related.title: Two odd Frobenius partners
related.detail: Lets d vary and studies two distinct odd partners in the unchanged retained set.

related.title: Same-set positive gain
related.detail: Follows that collision through selection, pricing, and the b′/4 row margin.

tracks.question: How do finite counts become fiber measures, and how does local mass enter Siegel–Weil?
tracks.finding: Track the modulus, vector lattice, and Haar convention alongside each number. Ramified target four is 257/128 in scalar normalization and 257/256 in the matched split-skew normalization.
